results.description:
# Medicare levy reduction for low-income earners A Medicare levy reduction applies if your taxable income is between the thresholds as a single low-income earner. **Last updated** 30 June 2026 Print or Download ## On this page - [When you don't pay the Medicare levy](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy/medicare-levy-reduction/medicare-levy-reduction-for-low-income-earners#ato-WhenyoudontpaytheMedicarelevy) - [Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy/medicare-levy-reduction/medicare-levy-reduction-for-low-income-earners#ato-Medicarelevyreductionthresholdsforsingles) ## When you don't pay the Medicare levy In 2025–26, you **don't** have to pay the Medicare levy if your taxable income is equal to or less than the lower Medicare levy threshold. Check the thresholds, see, [Table: Medicare levy thresholds for a single individual](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy/medicare-levy-reduction/medicare-levy-reduction-for-low-income-earners#Medicarelevyreductionthresholdssingletab). ## Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles Your taxable income must be equal to or less than the relevant upper threshold in the table for you to qualify for a reduction. We work out the reduction for you when you lodge your tax return. | Category | Lower
threshold | Upper
threshold | |-|-|-| | If you're entitled to the [Seniors and pensioners tax offset](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/income-deductions-offsets-and-records/tax-offsets/seniors-and-pensioners-tax-offset) | $44,268 | $55,335
(see [note 1](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy/medicare-levy-reduction/medicare-levy-reduction-for-low-income-earners#Note_1)) | | All other taxpayers | $28,011 | $35,013 | **Note 1**: The entitlement to the seniors and pensioners tax offset (SAPTO) for singles ceases when the rebate income reaches $52,759. If you don't qualify for a single reduction, you may still qualify for a reduction based on your [family taxable income](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy/medicare-levy-reduction/medicare-levy-reduction-family-income). If you don't qualify for a reduction in the Medicare levy, you may still qualify for a [Medicare levy exemption](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy/medicare-levy-exemption). You can use the [Medicare levy calculator](https://www.ato.gov.au/calculators-and-tools/tax-return-medicare-levy) to work out your Medicare levy payable. For prior year Medicare levy reduction thresholds, see: - [Medicare levy reduction threshold 2024–25](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/mytax-instructions/2025/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy-reduction-or-exemption) - [Medicare levy reduction threshold 2023–24](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/mytax-instructions/2024/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy-reduction-or-exemption) - [Medicare levy reduction threshold 2022–23](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/mytax-instructions/2023/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy-reduction-or-exemption) - [Medicare levy reduction threshold 2021–22](https://www.ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/your-tax-return/instructions-to-complete-your-tax-return/mytax-instructions/2022/medicare-and-private-health-insurance/medicare-levy-reduction-or-exemption) ### Example: Medicare levy reduction based on income within the threshold Angie's taxable income is $29,000. Angie is single with no dependants and she isn't entitled to SAPTO. Angie isn't eligible for any Medicare levy exemptions. Angie qualifies for a Medicare levy reduction because her taxable income is less than the upper threshold. Angie completes her tax return and we work out her Medicare levy reduction for her. Angie uses the Medicare levy calculator to find out how much Medicare levy she will pay. She enters her details and finds out her Medicare levy will be reduced to $98.90 End of example QC27031 Print or Download Report webpage issue ![Close](https://siteintercept.qualtrics.com/WRQualtricsShared/Graphics/siteintercept/wr-dialog-close-btn-black.png)

# Understanding the Medicare Levy
## What is the Medicare Levy?
However, if you’re a low-income earner, have a medical exemption or are a foreign resident, you may only have to pay a reduced rate or none at all.

## More information on the Medicare levy
### How much is the Medicare levy?
For lower-income earners, the ATO will determine the reduced Medicare levy rate you’ll pay.

### Who pays the Medicare levy?
Those earning between $28,011 and $35,013 pay a reduced rate less than 2%.

### Who’s exempt from paying the Medicare levy?
- **Low-income earners**. Anyone earning less than $28,011 in a financial year (or $44,268 for those who qualify for the SAPTO) won’t have to pay the Medicare levy.
